speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether an update can be provided on the review looking at how point-to-point services can better meet the evolving needs of commuters, including how effective a separate COE category for private-hire cars can support this endeavour; (b) what is the expected timeline for the completion of the review; and (c) under the review, whether occasional private-hire drivers who primarily use their vehicles for personal needs will be affected.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I understand that, as part of review, they will be studying the option of having a separate Certificate of Entitlement (COE) category for private hire vehicles.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If that is the case, will the separate COE category require additional regulations or licensing requirements and if so, how would this impact operational costs on new entrants into the sector?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But there are trade-offs with this idea and, therefore, we need to study this further.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, indeed, this is something that we are working on and studying.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But it is not something that we should take lightly.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Beyond that, as I have said in my main reply, the review for the P2P sector is not just about this idea of a special category or separate category for private hire cars, nor is it just purely about private hire cars.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It is about the P2P services, the industry structure and regulatory framework.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It covers the availability, resilience and inclusivity of P2P services, and how our rules and regulations should change to meet the needs of commuters and drivers.
